ticker.text: ▲ WHO: 9 CONFIRMED HONDIUS HANTAVIRUS CASES, 3 DEATHS; ANDES VIRUS CAUSE CONFIRMED
▲ AP: HONDIUS EN ROUTE ROTTERDAM FOR DISINFECTION; ARCTIC CRUISE SCHEDULE UNCERTAIN
► 2 AMERICAN HONDIUS PASSENGERS IN EMORY ATLANTA BIOCONTAINMENT SCDU; NO PUBLIC RISK
► ILLINOIS WINNEBAGO CO. RESIDENT SUSPECTED HANTAVIRUS AFTER RODENT CLEANUP; NOT HONDIUS
► FRANCE 42-DAY QUARANTINE DECREE; CRITICALLY ILL FRENCH WOMAN ON ECMO AT BICHAT PARIS
► 22 MONITORED INDIVIDUALS TRACKED GLOBALLY; 9 CONFIRMED CASES ACROSS MULTIPLE NATIONS
► ILLINOIS HANTAVIRUS STRAIN UNRELATED TO HONDIUS; NORTH AFRICAN VARIANT, NO H2H SPREAD
// EXPERTS: FUTURE HONDIUS PASSENGERS LIKELY SAFE; ANDES VIRUS POOR SURVIVABILITY SURFACES
// CDC LEVEL-3 EOC ACTIVE; US WHO DISENGAGEMENT CITED AS OUTBREAK RESPONSE VULNERABILITY
// WHO GLOBAL PUBLIC HEALTH RISK FROM HONDIUS HANTAVIRUS OUTBREAK ASSESSED AS LOW

sites.name: M/V HONDIUS
sites.desc: WHO confirmed 9 cases and 3 deaths as of 14 May; vessel docked Canary Islands to allow passenger evacuation to home countries. En route Rotterdam with skeleton crew of 30 + Dutch nurse for full disinfection; future Arctic cruise schedule uncertain pending health authority authorization per AP News.

sites.name: USHUAIA / ARGENTINA ROUTE
sites.desc: Index case (Dutch male, 70, died 11 Apr) took 4-month road trip 27 Nov 2025–1 Apr 2026 through Chile, Uruguay, Argentina before boarding. Argentine health ministry published detailed route map 06 May; Malbrán Institute trapping/testing rodents along route. Illumina sequencing shows Andes strain on Hondius has high similarity to Argentina 2018-19 strains per El País.

sites.name: SAINT HELENA
sites.desc: 30 passengers disembarked 24 Apr including Dutch index male's body and Dutch widow (later died Johannesburg) and Swiss confirmed male. UKHSA contact-tracing 30 disembarkees plus 82 pax and 6 crew from 25 Apr Airlink St Helena–Johannesburg flight. Four Tristan da Cunha islanders also transited St Helena aboard Hondius per UK minister Doughty.

sites.name: JOHANNESBURG
sites.desc: Case 2 (Dutch widow, 69, PCR+) died Johannesburg hospital 26 Apr — confirmed Andes virus fatality. Case 3 (British guide Martin Anstee, 56, PCR+) treated at Johannesburg ICU; improving, transferred Netherlands. A second British national confirmed PCR-positive 08 May in a South Africa health facility. NICD contact-traced 65+ contacts from 25 Apr Airlink flight.

sites.name: AMSTERDAM / NIJMEGEN / ROTTERDAM
sites.desc: British Case 3 (Anstee) transferred to Netherlands after improving in South Africa. Dutch crew member (41, confirmed) treated at Radboud UMC Nijmegen. Netherlands lab PCR-confirmed German woman died of Andes virus. MV Hondius sailing to Rotterdam post-Tenerife for full disinfection with skeleton crew of 30 + Dutch nurse aboard.

sites.name: MANCHESTER / WIRRAL / LONDON
sites.desc: 22 British nationals evacuated Tenerife; 20 flew Titan Airways charter to Manchester, now at Arrowe Park Hospital (Wirral) for up to 72-hr clinical assessment + testing, then 45-day self-isolation. UKHSA: 3 British cases total — 2 PCR-confirmed (SA/NL) + 1 suspected Tristan da Cunha. British Army parachute drop on Tristan da Cunha (9 May) in support of suspected case there.

sites.name: PARIS / LE BOURGET
sites.desc: First confirmed hantavirus case in France: one of five repatriated Hondius passengers tested PCR-positive; critically ill French woman now on artificial lung (ECMO) at Bichat Hospital Paris per AP 12 May. French government mandated 42-day quarantine decree with contact tracing identifying 22 potential cases across international flights.

sites.name: ZURICH / GENEVA
sites.desc: PCR-confirmed male passenger disembarked St Helena 24 Apr; symptoms onset 01 May, tested positive Andes virus 05 May at University Hospital Zurich. Illumina sequencing at Zurich and Geneva laboratories confirmed Andes variant with high similarity to Argentina 2018-19 strains and no new mutations per El País. Wife asymptomatic and isolating; Swiss contact tracing ongoing.

sites.name: BERLIN / DÜSSELDORF
sites.desc: German woman died on board 02 May (fever/malaise onset 28 Apr, pneumonia); Netherlands postmortem PCR confirmed Andes virus. German nationals repatriated via Dutch charter from Tenerife 10 May. Asymptomatic 65-year-old German contact tested NEGATIVE; RKI contact tracing active.

sites.name: ALICANTE
sites.desc: 32-year-old woman (seated 2 rows behind deceased Dutch woman on 25 Apr Airlink flight) returned first PCR NEGATIVE at Centro Nacional de Microbiología. Awaiting second confirmatory PCR; if also negative, transfers to Gómez Ulla Military Hospital Madrid.

sites.name: TENERIFE
sites.desc: Hondius docked Granadilla de Abona port 10 May concluding 40-day health crisis; 152 disembarked in successful 23-nation evacuation praised by WHO per El País. One Spanish passenger tested PCR-positive post-disembarkation (12 May, El País); patient asymptomatic, confirmatory PCR pending. Spanish inspectors confirmed no rodents found aboard vessel.

sites.name: MADRID
sites.desc: Spanish nationals were the first nationality evacuated from Tenerife per AP News, landing Torrejón de Ardoz military airport and transported to Gómez Ulla Military Hospital. No Spanish nationals showing symptoms at disembarkation; PCR on arrival + Day 7 with twice-daily temperature monitoring.

sites.name: BARCELONA
sites.desc: Two Barcelona contacts monitored: (1) South African woman (asymptomatic flight contact of Dutch deceased) spent ~1 week here before returning South Africa — confirmed asymptomatic. (2) Barcelona-resident woman identified 09 May as flight contact after mid-flight seat change; asymptomatic, under official monitoring per Spanish Health Ministry.

sites.name: TRISTAN DA CUNHA
sites.desc: UKHSA confirmed suspected case 08 May: British male islander aboard Hondius during 13–15 Apr stop; symptoms onset 28 Apr, stable in isolation on island. RAF A400M emergency airdrop 09 May: 6 paratroopers + 2 military clinicians parachuted onto island's golf course delivering 3.3 tonnes medical supplies — first-ever UK military humanitarian parachute deployment.

sites.name: SINGAPORE
sites.desc: CLEARED 09 May: Both male residents (aged 67 and 65) tested NEGATIVE for hantavirus including Andes virus via multiple PCR samples — Singapore CDA confirmed. Both had disembarked Hondius at St Helena and traveled on 25 Apr Airlink flight. Monitoring continues through full incubation window.

sites.name: ONTARIO
sites.desc: Two Ontario residents self-isolating — Hondius passengers who returned home early, asymptomatic. Canadian repatriation flight departed Tenerife 10 May per AP News (second nationality after Spain to evacuate). PHAC coordinating monitoring per 07 May government statement.

sites.name: QUEBEC
sites.desc: One Quebec resident self-isolating — not a Hondius passenger but shared homebound flight with two Canadian Hondius disembarkees. Asymptomatic; PHAC monitoring active.

sites.name: ARIZONA
sites.desc: ADHS monitoring one returning passenger under 42-day observation. Asymptomatic as of 13 May. CDC notified ADHS 05 May; public risk assessed as very low. Part of domestic US monitoring cohort across 6 states.

sites.name: CALIFORNIA
sites.desc: CDPH monitoring one returned Hondius traveler via daily temperature checks and symptom assessment. A second California resident transited Tenerife to Nebraska NQU via CDC/HHS biocontainment charter. No California residents reported ill as of 13 May. Acting CDC Director Bhattacharya criticised on CNN for vague responses on hantavirus passenger monitoring procedures per The Daily Beast.

sites.name: GEORGIA
sites.desc: Two American Hondius passengers transferred to Emory University Hospital SCDU in Atlanta for monitoring as of 12 May per Axios; two additional Georgia residents asymptomatic and following CDC guidance at home. Emory stated no public risk anticipated; SCDU, established 2002, is one of few US facilities capable of treating dangerous communicable diseases.

sites.name: TEXAS
sites.desc: Texas DSHS monitoring two returning Hondius passengers. Both asymptomatic as of 13 May. Part of domestic US monitoring cohort across 6 states.

sites.name: VIRGINIA
sites.desc: VDH monitoring one returning Hondius passenger. Asymptomatic. CDC classified response as Level-3; Emergency Operations Center activated. Six states — AZ, CA, GA, TX, VA, NJ — monitoring at least 9 early-disembarkees or contacts.

sites.name: NEW JERSEY
sites.desc: NJ DOH monitoring two individuals potentially exposed to a Hondius passenger post-disembarkation during air travel. Neither symptomatic as of 13 May. Exposure occurred during air travel abroad; residents were not Hondius passengers themselves.

sites.name: NEBRASKA
sites.desc: Nebraska Medicine / UNMC NQU received Dr. Stephen Kornfeld (Oregon oncologist, PCR-positive) after he assisted ill Hondius passengers aboard; a second symptomatic American also in biocontainment. 17 Americans quarantined in Omaha with two requiring biocontainment due to mild symptoms per The Daily Beast; CDC says widespread US transmission unlikely.

sites.name: UTAH
sites.desc: Utah DHHS confirmed at least one Utah resident among the Americans aboard MV Hondius. Person asymptomatic; disembarked Tenerife with federal escort to Nebraska NQU for evaluation. No Utah residents monitored at home as of 13 May.

sites.name: ILLINOIS
sites.desc: Winnebago County resident suspected of contracting hantavirus (North African variant, not Andes) after cleaning a rodent-infested property per The Daily Beast; health officials believe exposure via aerosolized rat urine or feces. Case assessed as unrelated to MV Hondius outbreak; showing mild symptoms, not hospitalized, and recovering per The Daily Beast.

sites.name: MANILA
sites.desc: 38 Filipino crew members aboard Hondius; Philippines DOH confirmed none currently ill as of 13 May. Skeleton crew of ~30 (predominantly Filipino) will remain aboard to sail vessel to Rotterdam with Dutch nurse. Monitoring continues through incubation window.

sites.name: DUBLIN / BALDONNELL
sites.desc: Irish passengers repatriated 10 May via Defence Forces Dassault Falcon 6X government jet to Baldonnell — first medevac mission for the aircraft (acquired Dec 2025, €53M). Irish Dept of Health National Incident Management Team stood up; coordinating with ECDC, HSE. No symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: PRAIA
sites.desc: Hondius anchored Praia 03–06 May; refused docking by Cape Verde per The Week. Three medevac patients evacuated 06 May — two flew Amsterdam (hazmat teams at Schiphol), third plane made unscheduled Gran Canaria refueling stop after Morocco refused permission + medical equipment malfunction. Dr. Stephen Kornfeld (oncologist aboard) coordinated with global health experts during this period per The Atlantic.

sites.name: COPENHAGEN
sites.desc: Danish Patient Safety Authority confirmed one Danish national was aboard MV Hondius. Person returned to Denmark end of April, self-isolating, no symptoms, not in close contact with any confirmed case. Monitoring active per national protocol.

sites.name: BRUSSELS
sites.desc: Belgian nationals repatriated via Dutch charter from Tenerife (10 May Sunday flight alongside NL/DE/GR nationals) per AP News repatriation sequence. Belgian federal health authorities coordinating with ECDC. No symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: WELLINGTON
sites.desc: NZ nationals among passengers on final Australia-led repatriation flight departing Tenerife Monday afternoon. NZ Ministry of Health coordinating contact tracing; no symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: STOCKHOLM
sites.desc: Sweden confirmed among 12+ countries monitoring Hondius nationals who disembarked. Swedish Public Health Agency (Folkhälsomyndigheten) coordinating; no symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: ANKARA
sites.desc: Turkish nationals evacuated Tenerife 10 May per AP News multi-nation repatriation sequence. Turkish Ministry of Health coordinating; no symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: BASSETERRE
sites.desc: Saint Kitts and Nevis confirmed among 12+ countries monitoring nationals who disembarked MV Hondius. Local health authorities monitoring; no symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: ATHENS
sites.desc: Greek nationals repatriated via Dutch charter from Tenerife (10 May Sunday flight alongside NL/DE/BE nationals). Greek Ministry of Health coordinating with ECDC; no symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: WARSAW
sites.desc: Polish nationals confirmed aboard Hondius per ECDC briefing. Polish Chief Sanitary Inspectorate coordinating with ECDC; no symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: LISBON
sites.desc: Portuguese nationals confirmed aboard Hondius per ECDC briefing. DGS Portugal coordinating with ECDC; no symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: SYDNEY / CANBERRA
sites.desc: Australia sending repatriation plane for final Tenerife flight Monday afternoon covering Australian, New Zealand, and several Asian-country nationals per AP News. At least one Australian national had disembarked at Saint Helena 24 Apr and returned home. Australian health authorities monitoring; no symptomatic cases reported.
